clue.text: New edict she made for the house

indicators.note: new here means remade, so the letters of the three words are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A freshly issued decree from her concerns a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a common British dwelling sharing one wall with its neighbour, a type of home.

clue.text: English brains reform the language

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: English brains are urged to reform the language.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slavic tongue spoken in Belgrade and the Balkans.

clue.text: Intend to take the continental, circuitous journey?

parts.note: to intend is to mean
der is the German for the, German being a continental language

explanation.surface: A traveller plans a roundabout continental trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' points to a European language: DER is German for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A winding route or ramble, from the twisting river in Asia Minor.

clue.text: Light heart in the welfare building

parts.note: daylight, so light is day
the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: A lamp glows at the heart of the welfare office.
explanation.definitionFit: A place offering daytime social care for the elderly or disabled is a welfare facility.

clue.text: Harris's river?

parts.note: the cloth woven on Harris in the Hebrides shares its name with the river on the Scottish border

explanation.surface: Asking which river belongs to someone called Harris.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris is an island in the Outer Hebrides famous for its woollen cloth; the same name is a river on the England-Scotland border.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris cloth is a rough woollen fabric, and the same word is a Border river.

clue.text: Tom' well, perhaps, in French bottling-premises

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, chat in French
a well gives water, eau in French

explanation.surface: A French tomcat at a well, near a bottling plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in French' applies to both pieces: cat is CHAT, water EAU. Bordeaux wine is labelled as bottled at the estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A French wine estate where the vintage is bottled on site, as on Bordeaux labels.

clue.text: Anglo-American side on the ball

parts.note: in American pool, spin put on the cue ball is named after Britain's main nation, so the term is Anglo yet American

explanation.surface: A transatlantic football team is playing well.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sports team; in American billiards the word for spin is the same as the British adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call sidespin on a billiard ball by the adjective for the people of England.

clue.text: Her Majesty's production controller?

parts.note: Her Majesty's is a London theatre, so the person running its shows backstage

explanation.surface: A royal official supervising the output of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Her Majesty's Theatre is in London's West End; the 'production' is a play, run backstage by this person.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running a play backstage controls the show during performance.

clue.text: Harris's pitched-up delivery

parts.note: Joel Chandler Harris wrote the Uncle Remus tales; the figure there is a doll of pitch, read as a delivered infant made of tar

explanation.surface: Harris bowls a ball pitched up to the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cricketer called Harris; 'pitched' is tar and 'delivery' a newborn, giving the sticky doll that traps Brer Rabbit in Harris's Uncle Remus stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The sticky figure in the Uncle Remus folk tales is a doll smeared with pitch, made to catch the rabbit.

clue.text: Basic teaching no good in sabbatical that is set back

indicators.note: the two letters for no and good are placed in the middle of the other piece
set back asks for the word for sabbatical to be read from its end to its start

parts.note: a sabbatical is a period of leave

explanation.surface: A sabbatical spent badly sets someone back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns LEAVE into EVAEL, and 'in' puts NG inside it after EVA.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangel is a gospel, the core doctrine or message of a faith.

clue.text: Time lines with gaiety, perhaps, when actors play thus

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are reordered

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A theatre schedule weighs time spent on lines against fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Legitimate theatre is serious drama as opposed to variety, hence actors performing that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit theatre is straight drama, so actors performing proper plays perform in this manner.

clue.text: Elgar's middle enigma can be hot for a bass

definitions.text: can be hot for a bass

indicators.note: the middle of the composer's name means only its central letter is kept

parts.note: an enigma is a puzzle or riddle, a nod to the Enigma Variations

explanation.surface: Elgar's Enigma Variations hide a part that suits a bass singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The bass is a fish, not a singer: a flat iron plate gets hot to cook it.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat cooking plate is heated so food such as fish can be fried on it.

clue.text: Considering English flower-pottery?

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Dee runs through England and Wales
Ming is the fine Chinese porcelain of that dynasty

explanation.surface: Someone is weighing up English flowerpots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river, here the Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to judge or think, so judging is the sense of considering.

clue.text: Junior, we hear, of forty-nine

indicators.note: we hear means the clue word's synonym is to be spoken and a word of the same sound written

parts.note: a junior is a minor, someone under age

explanation.surface: A young person seems to belong to a group of forty-nine.
explanation.walkthrough: The forty-niners were gold diggers of the 1849 California rush, as in the song Clementine.
explanation.definitionFit: A forty-niner was a gold digger in the 1849 California rush, a man working claims underground.

clue.text: One of the slings of O.F? Ay, there's the rub, etc — outrageous!

definitions.text: One of the slings of O.F

indicators.note: outrageous suggests wild disorder, so the letters before it are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Hamlet's soliloquy is misquoted: slings, outrageous fortune, the rub.
explanation.walkthrough: O.F. is outrageous fortune, whose slings Hamlet mentions; 'outrageous' also tells you to rearrange THE RUB ETC. The siege engine is a giant sling.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval siege engine hurled stones with a pivoting arm, a giant catapult of the sling kind.

clue.text: Make permanent institute

definitions.meaning: to fix something firmly in place

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to set something up so it lasts: fix firmly, and found an organisation.

clue.text: Times factor?

parts.note: a factor is an agent, so this is someone who acts as agent for the Times and other papers

explanation.surface: A mathematical question about what multiplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like multiplication and 'factor' its partner, but the Times is a newspaper and a factor a dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells papers deals in the Times among other dailies.

clue.text: Saw up tree trunk left as, refuse

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word saw is read from the bottom, backwards
trunk here means cut short, so the word tree loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone saws up a tree trunk and leaves it as waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SAW to WAS; 'trunk' docks tree to TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant waste matter, rubbish, before coming to mean a good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Tumbler often seen on bars

parts.note: a tumbler sounds like a drinking glass in a pub, but is a gymnast working on parallel bars

explanation.surface: A glass commonly found on pub counters.
explanation.walkthrough: Tumbler and bars both suggest a pub; the gymnast performs on the bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast or circus performer doing somersaults and balancing feats.

clue.text: Colonizers on the move south become enthusiastic

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
to warm to something is to become keen on it

explanation.surface: Settlers heading south grow keen on the venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees leave the hive in a mass to found a new colony elsewhere.

clue.text: Post-Impressionist?

parts.note: not an artist after Monet but one who makes impressions on post, inking marks on mail

explanation.surface: A painter of the school after Impressionism.
explanation.walkthrough: The art movement is a decoy: post office workers impress marks on letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker or device that inks a postmark onto letters.

clue.text: Squinting in mask ancestors used

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words mask ancestors

explanation.surface: Squinting through masks ancestors wore.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to glance sideways, eyes narrowed in suspicion.

clue.text: Georgia's underdone caper gives such stomach trouble

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia, plus the 's

indicators.note: underdone means not finished, so the word for caper loses its final letter

parts.note: a caper is a prank or trick

explanation.surface: A half-cooked dish in Georgia upsets the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Caper looks like the pickled bud on a plate; it is a trick, cut short by 'underdone' to TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of the belly, so stomach trouble is described with this word.

clue.text: One embraced by quaint attractive girl

indicators.note: embraced by means the word for one is held inside the word for quaint

parts.note: quaint means cute
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is hugged by a quaint pretty girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretty, appealing young woman, in American slang.

clue.text: Skinny in wager that is put on a horse

definitions.text: that is put on a horse

indicators.note: in shows the word for skinny goes inside the word for wager

parts.note: a wager is a bet
skinny means thin, lank

explanation.surface: A thin bet is placed on a horse at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on a horse' suggests betting, but it is a rug thrown over the animal's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug for horses is a covering laid on the animal's back for warmth.

clue.text: Fashion arbiter of Welsh taste

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape, so the letters of the next word are reshaped

explanation.surface: A style guru judges Welsh cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion arbiter' reads as a trendsetter; Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a cheese-on-toast dish, a savoury snack from Wales.

clue.text: I am contracted to join board and enrol jury

parts.note: I am shortened gives the contraction I'm
a board is a panel, a committee

explanation.surface: Someone signs a contract to join a board and sign up a jury.
explanation.definitionFit: To list or swear in jurors is to draw them up on a roster for a trial.

clue.text: You can put your shirt on it

definitions.text: You can put your shirt on it

parts.words: You can put your shirt on it
parts.note: putting your shirt on a horse means betting everything; here a shirt literally hangs on a drying frame

explanation.surface: A tipster urges you to bet everything on a sure winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is racing slang for an all-in bet; the 'horse' is a wooden frame for drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden drying frame is a stand where laundry hangs, a domestic rack.
